title: Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program Authorization Standard: Written Orders, Prior Authorization and Grants
content:
Every shipment on the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program rests on a written order from the treating prescriber that names the item, the billing units per 30 days, the order date and the prescriber's NPI.

## 1. The written order

1.1 The order is valid for the tier's order validity period in calendar months counted from its order date, the valid-through date being the day before the same calendar day that many months later (falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist), and Larkfield records that valid-through date when the order is received.

1.2 A written order on file for the item is required before a prior authorization request is submitted and before an authorization grant is recorded; this is read from Larkfield's order records, matched to the order concerned.

*Hypothetical example:* with a 12-month validity period, an order dated 2026-03-10 is valid through 2027-03-09.

## 2. Tiers where prior authorization is required

2.1 On tiers where prior authorization is required, Larkfield submits a prior authorization request to the payer once the written order is on file and moves the program from referral received to pending authorization.

2.2 The payer's approval is recorded as an authorization grant with basis payer prior authorization, carrying the payer's PA reference, the approved units and the approved span, which runs the tier's prior authorization validity period (the figure listed as formulary exception validity) in calendar months from the decision date unless the payer's approval states an earlier valid-through date, in which case the payer's date governs.

## 3. Tiers where prior authorization is not required

On tiers where prior authorization is not required, Larkfield records the authorization grant itself on the basis of the written order (basis written order, or self-pay order on the self-pay tier), valid from the order date through the order's valid-through date, for the billing units the order covers within that span.

## 4. Standard and expedited requests

A prior authorization request is submitted as expedited only when the prescriber states on the order that waiting the standard decision time could seriously jeopardize the patient's life or health; otherwise it is standard, and the payer is expected to decide within the tier's standard decision time in calendar days of a standard request or the tier's expedited decision time in hours of an expedited one.

## 5. Renewal requests

A renewal request for a prior authorization may be submitted no earlier than the tier's renewal lead in calendar days before the valid-through date of the authorization it renews, counted backward in calendar days from that valid-through date with the earliest submission day itself allowed, and it requires a written order that is valid beyond that valid-through date.

| Hypothetical case (renewal lead of 30 days; authorization valid through 2026-09-30) | Renewal request may be submitted? |
|---|---|
| Submitted 2026-08-30 | No — earlier than 30 calendar days before the valid-through date |
| Submitted 2026-08-31 | Yes — the earliest submission day itself is allowed |
| Submitted 2026-09-15, written order valid through 2026-09-30 | No — the order is not valid beyond the valid-through date being renewed |
| Submitted 2026-09-15, written order valid through 2027-03-09 | Yes |

## 6. Activation

A program is activated only when an authorization grant on file for the program is valid on the activation date. Activation moves the program from referral received or pending authorization to active, and refills may then ship.

## 7. Denials

A payer denial of a prior authorization is recorded with the payer's denial reason; the program stays in pending authorization while the prescriber supplies further documentation or a new request is made, and it closes only under the program's hold and closure rules.

## 8. Clinical documents

Clinical documents are recorded with the purpose they serve and the visit date they document, and a document serves only the purpose recorded on it.
